articles.title: Durigan fala em ajuste nas contas públicas após piora do mercado | G1
articles.standfirst: BC divulgou nesta terça o 1º boletim com projeções para a economia após a reeleição de Lula. Na semana passada, índice da Bolsa, juros futuros e câmbio já haviam registrado piora.
articles.summary: Dario Durigan defende ajuste gradual das contas públicas e rebate o pessimismo do mercado após novas projeções de inflação e juros no Boletim Focus.
articles.body:
Com a piora das expectativas do mercado financeiro, após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, disse ter compromisso com a melhora da trajetória das contas públicas brasileiras nos próximos anos, mas sem recorrer ao que ele chamou de "narrativa fácil" da oposição

Mais cedo, nesta terça-feira, o Banco Central divulgou seu boletim semanal com projeções dos economistas dos bancos sobre a economia brasileira.

➡️Em linhas gerais, os analistas elevaram consideravelmente suas projeções de inflação, reduziram as expectativas de crescimento da economia e passaram a prever uma taxa de juros mais elevada do que antes. As estimativas para o dólar também subiram bastante.

➡️ O documento foi divulgado após expressivos ajustes registrados na semana passada em ativos brasileiros, como o índice da Bolsa de Valores, os juros futuros e o dólar, que já haviam mostrado piora após a confirmação de que Lula será presidente do país nos próximos quatro anos.

"O projeto que o presidente Lula apresentou, e saiu vitorioso das urnas, é um projeto generoso com o país, que se compromete com as diferentes classes e diferentes categorias e, ao mesmo tempo, com melhora fiscal. Esse é um grande desafio que nós vamos ter que achar: o caminho para fazer essas duas coisas, sem procurar uma narrativa fácil como o candidato perdedor fazia, ou sem apresentar projetos que não levaram a nada", disse o ministro Durigan.

▶️Analistas têm manifestado reiteradamente preocupação com a trajetória das contas públicas. Eles avaliam que os reiterados déficits fiscais dos últimos anos pressionam a taxa de juros, e consequentemente, o endividamento público.

Para baixar o juro e conter a dívida, cobram um ajuste fiscal mais forte por parte do governo.

▶️O mercado tem se mostrado reticente sobre a possibilidade de um ajuste de grande proporção e rápido nas contas públicas prometido diante dos compromissos assumidos de manter os programas sociais, de aumentar acima da inflação do salário mínimo, assim como das aposentadorias, e de não promover cortes profundos em áreas como saúde, educação.

O ministro da Fazenda tem afirmado que o objetivo da proposta do PT é de promover um ajuste gradual das contas públicas, da ordem de dois pontos do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) , no quarto mandato do presidente Lula. Ele tem reafirmado que as contas retornarão ao azul em 2027, após permanecerem deficitárias durante todo o atual mandato de Lula.

"O que eu posso assegurar é que nós vamos seguir uma trajetória de melhorar as contas públicas do país, melhorar o resultado primário, como nós fizemos de 2023 para cá", disse o ministro da Fazenda.

"Fazendo com rigor a avaliação das políticas públicas já existentes, de não para tirar direitos, mas para garantir que o dinheiro público seja bem aplicado e olhar para os investimentos estratégicos do país, melhorando a governança do governo", completou Durigan.

Questionado por jornalistas, ele afirmou que não tem discutido a política de sucessão no Ministério da Fazenda, se haverá troca de ministro.

"Esse é o 'timing' do presidente que eu obedeço, tá? Tenho apresentado propostas, diagnósticos e propostas com críticas, algumas propostas fáceis que aparecem e reforçando a trajetória do que eu acredito, que é melhorar as condições de vida das pessoas, melhorar a condição fiscal que ajuda a melhorar a condição de vida das pessoas", concluiu.

Dario Durigan, ministro da Fazenda — Foto: Washington Costa/MF

articles.title: Disney planeja milhares de demissões e cobra redução de 20% nos custos | G1
articles.standfirst: Companhia pediu a gestores que busquem economia anual de 20% nas despesas; número de funcionários que poderão ser demitidos ainda não foi informado.
articles.summary: Companhia pediu a gestores que busquem economia anual de 20% nas despesas; número de funcionários que poderão ser demitidos ainda não foi informado.
articles.body:
Disney corta empregos em meio à crise — Foto: REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

A Disney pediu a gestores que reduzam em 20% os custos sob sua responsabilidade e avalia demitir milhares de funcionários , segundo informações da Bloomberg publicadas nesta segunda-feira (2). O número de demissões ainda não foi definido.

A iniciativa seria parte de um esforço de reestruturação da companhia, que enfrenta desafios como o avanço da inteligência artificial, a queda da receita de bilheteria , a concorrência no mercado de streaming e a desaceleração do público internacional em seus parques temáticos.

Segundo a Bloomberg, algumas áreas da empresa deverão arcar com uma parcela maior dos cortes do que outras.

➡️ Parte da economia obtida com a redução de despesas deverá ser reinvestida em produções de cinema e televisão, tecnologia, parques temáticos e negócios de cruzeiros.

🎥 Na prática, a companhia quer que gestores encontrem maneiras de gastar menos para manter suas operações , seja com revisão de despesas, reorganização de equipes ou outros ajustes

A Disney tinha cerca de 231 mil funcionários no fim do ano fiscal de 2025.

A companhia vem promovendo cortes de pessoal nos últimos anos para melhorar sua rentabilidade.

Em setembro, a Disney demitiu algumas centenas de funcionários das áreas de recursos humanos e tecnologia. Em abril, a companhia já havia eliminado cerca de mil vagas em diferentes setores, incluindo marketing, estúdios, televisão e ESPN.

🔍 Em 2023, a empresa anunciou o corte de 7 mil vagas como parte de um plano para economizar US$ 5,5 bilhões em despesas.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026: brasileiros estão mais exigentes e buscam descontos maiores, diz pesquisa da Globo | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa da Globo mostra que 65% dos brasileiros esperam descontos melhores que em 2025, mas intenção de compra caiu de 47% para 36%; 75% dos indecisos admitem compras por impulso diante de boas ofertas.
articles.summary: Pesquisa da Globo mostra que 65% dos brasileiros esperam descontos melhores que em 2025, mas intenção de compra caiu de 47% para 36%.
articles.body:
Como empreendedores se preparam para faturar mais na Black Friday — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

A expectativa dos consumidores brasileiros por ofertas melhores na Black Friday deste ano aumentou, mas a disposição para comprar diminuiu.

É o que mostra a segunda onda de uma pesquisa da Globo, realizada com 2 mil pessoas entre 6 e 9 de outubro de 2026. Na comparação com o levantamento anterior, feito em junho, a parcela de consumidores que espera encontrar descontos melhores do que no ano passado passou de 53% para 65%.

Além disso, 84% afirmam que só compram se encontrarem preços realmente menores do que em outros períodos.

Apesar da queda na intenção declarada de compra, de 47% para 36%, há espaço para atrair consumidores que ainda não decidiram se vão às compras: 75% dos indecisos ou daqueles que não pretendem comprar admitem que podem fazer uma compra não planejada durante a data.

"O que vemos é um consumidor mais exigente, que está disposto a comprar, mas quer ter certeza de que está diante de uma boa oportunidade", afirma Eliseu Barreira, diretor de Estratégia e Inteligência de Negócios da Globo.

Segundo ele, o desafio para marcas e varejistas é transformar a expectativa por descontos em uma percepção concreta de vantagem.

Entre os consumidores indecisos, 54% dizem que descontos relevantes poderiam levá-los a comprar. Outros 39% mencionam frete grátis, enquanto 23% apontam condições facilitadas de pagamento.

"O preço continua sendo determinante, mas não é o único elemento dessa decisão. A oportunidade precisa fazer sentido como um todo, considerando também conveniência, confiança e experiência de compra", diz Barreira.

A pesquisa também mostra que os consumidores estão antecipando as decisões de compra.

A parcela dos que começam a pesquisar produtos três meses antes da Black Friday passou de 28% para 38% entre as duas ondas do levantamento. Além disso, 32% afirmam que comprariam antes de novembro caso encontrassem uma oferta muito boa , ante 24% em junho.

Na direção contrária, caiu de 32% para 25% a parcela dos consumidores que pretende esperar especificamente pela sexta-feira da Black Friday para fazer compras.

Para Barreira, a mudança reforça que a data deixou de ser apenas um dia de promoções e passou a representar um período mais longo de pesquisa, comparação de preços e decisões. "As marcas precisam estar presentes ao longo de todo esse percurso", afirma.

À medida que a Black Friday se aproxima, algumas categorias de produtos também ganham força entre os consumidores. O interesse por eletrônicos avançou de 20% para 29% entre junho e outubro.

Vestuário passou de 20% para 27%; eletrodomésticos , de 23% para 27%; e produtos de autocuidado , de 14% para 22%.

Apesar do avanço das intenções por determinadas categorias, a escolha das marcas ainda está em aberto. Apenas 13% dos consumidores já decidiram exatamente quais produtos e marcas pretendem comprar.

"Mesmo quando o consumidor já sabe qual categoria deseja, a escolha da marca pode acontecer mais adiante", diz Barreira. Segundo ele, esse cenário abre espaço para que as empresas conquistem a preferência dos clientes até os momentos mais próximos da compra.

Além dos preços, a confiança também pesa na decisão. De acordo com o levantamento, 40% dos consumidores priorizam lojas nas quais já tiveram boas experiências de compra, enquanto 32% consideram as avaliações de outros consumidores.

Barreira afirma que a decisão não depende apenas do desconto anunciado. A reputação da loja, o frete e o prazo de entrega também influenciam a escolha. "O consumidor não avalia apenas o desconto. Ele considera a segurança da compra e a experiência que terá com aquela marca", explica.

Para o executivo, a principal lição da pesquisa é que as empresas precisam considerar todo o caminho percorrido pelo consumidor, desde as primeiras buscas até a decisão final.

"O consumidor pesquisa com antecedência, compara preços, considera diferentes marcas e pode mudar sua decisão diante de uma oportunidade relevante", afirma.

A pesquisa integra o trabalho de inteligência da Globo para acompanhar hábitos e comportamentos dos brasileiros. Os resultados também servem de base para o Globo Friday , projeto comercial da empresa que reúne ações na TV Globo , em canais pagos, plataformas digitais e no Globoplay .

Em 2026, a iniciativa inclui o Momento Globo Friday , que leva a experiência da Black Friday aos intervalos comerciais da TV Globo durante todo o mês de novembro.

O projeto também prevê o uso de soluções tecnológicas, como os Plugins Ao Vivo do Globoplay, para ampliar as possibilidades de conexão entre anunciantes e consumidores.

articles.title: Após reeleição de Lula, mercado financeiro vê inflação mais alta e piora previsão para taxa de juros e dólar | G1
articles.standfirst: Expectativas são divulgadas toda semana pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada com mais de 100 instituições financeiras. Recorte de agora faz referência à semana passada.
articles.summary: Expectativas são divulgadas toda semana pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada com mais de 100 instituições financeiras. Recorte de agora faz referência à semana passada.
articles.body:
Após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) em 25 de outubro, os economistas do mercado financeiro realizaram fortes ajustes em suas expectativas para a inflação, taxa de juros e para o crescimento da economia neste ano e nos próximos.

➡️Em linhas gerais, os analistas elevaram consideravelmente suas projeções de inflação , reduziram as expectativas de crescimento da economia e passaram a prever uma taxa de juros mais elevada do que antes. As estimativas para o dólar também subiram bastante.

As informações fazem parte do "Boletim Focus", divulgado nesta terça-feira (3) pelo Banco Central (BC), com base em pesquisa realizada na última semana com mais de 100 instituições financeiras.

➡️ Para 2026, a estimativa de inflação cresceu de 5,19% para 5,22%;

➡️ Para 2027, a expectativa subiu de 4,34% para 4,76%;

➡️ Para 2028, a previsão permaneceu em 3,75% para 4%;

➡️ Para 2029, a estimativa avançou de 3,50% para 3,98%.

🔎 Por que isso importa? Quanto maior a inflação, menor é o poder de compra da população — especialmente entre quem recebe salários mais baixos. Isso ocorre porque os preços sobem, enquanto os salários não acompanham esse aumento.

Para o crescimento do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) deste ano, o mercado financeiro reduziu sua estimativa de 1,80% para 1,76% na semana passada.

Com isso, os analistas estimam desaceleração da economia neste ano , visto que, em 2025, o PIB cresceu 2,3% , conforme divulgação oficial do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ).

➡️ O Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) é a soma de todos os bens e serviços produzidos no país e serve para medir o desempenho da economia.

🔎Se o PIB cresce, significa que a economia vai bem e produz mais. Se o PIB cai, quer dizer que a economia está encolhendo. Entretanto, nem sempre crescimento do PIB equivale a bem-estar social.

Para 2027, a projeção do mercado de crescimento do PIB caiu de 1,31% para 1,20%.

Para 2028, a estimativa do mercado para a expansão da economia recuou de 1,81% para 1,80%.

Em um ano eleitoral, o governo tem adotado ações para estimular a economia e reduzir o endividamento da população, o que impulsiona a demanda por produtos e serviços.

A estratégia do governo, porém, dificulta o controle da inflação. O BC tem dito claramente que uma desaceleração, ou seja, um ritmo menor de crescimento da economia, faz parte da estratégia de conter as pressões inflacionárias.

Após reeleição de Lula, mercado financeiro vê inflação mais alta e piora bastante previsão para taxa de juros e dólar. — Foto: Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

O mercado financeiro também manteve a projeção de cortes na taxa de juros neste ano, mas reduziu sua projeção de redução da Selic. As estimativas para os próximos anos também foram ajustadas para cima.

A estimativa do mercado para a taxa Selic ao fim de 2026 subiu de 13,25% para 13,50% ao ano na última semana, embutindo somente uma nova redução neste ano, ao invés de duas.

Para o fechamento de 2027, a projeção do mercado subiu de 11,75% para 12,5% ao ano.

Para o fim de 2028, a estimativa dos analistas avançou de 10% para 11% ao ano.

Para o fim de 2029, a expectativa dos analistas passou de 10% para 10,25% ao ano

O mercado financeiro baixou sua estimativa para a taxa de câmbio ao fim deste ano de R$ 5,05 para R$ 5,34 por dólar.

Para o fechamento de 2027, a projeção dos economistas dos bancos subiu de R$ 5,15 para R$ 5,40 por dólar.

Para o fim de 2028, a expectativa do mercado para o dólar passou de R$ 5,20 para R$ 5,40.

Já para o fechamento de 2029, avançou de R$ 5,28 para R$ 5,45 por dólar.

articles.title: Ministro diz que proposta para 'imposto do pecado' deve ser enviada nesta terça ao Congresso; objetivo é manter carga em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta prevê manutenção da atual carga tributária sobre os produtos que causam danos à saúde no próximo ano, período de transição. Posteriormente, a partir de 2028, ideia é que taxação aumente.
articles.summary: Proposta prevê manutenção da atual carga tributária sobre os produtos que causam danos à saúde no próximo ano, período de transição. Posteriormente, a partir de 2028, ideia é que taxação aumente.
articles.body:
O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, informou nesta terça-feira (3) que tem reunião agendada hoje com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) para discutir a medida provisória (MP) do Imposto Seletivo, também conhecido como "imposto do pecado".

Segundo ele, a proposta, que pode ser enviada ainda nesta terça ao Congresso Nacional, prevê a manutenção da atual carga tributária sobre os produtos que causam danos à saúde no próximo ano , período de transição. Posteriormente, a partir de 2028, a ideia é que a taxação aumente.

"A MP já saiu aqui do Ministério da Fazenda, eu devo despachar como presidente hoje, tá? Então a expectativa é que seja hoje, sim [o envio ao Congresso Nacional] (...). Ela tem que ser aprovada até o fim do ano", declarou o ministro a jornalistas. Segundo ele, a MP está atualmente na Casa Civil.

Durigan confirmou que fez um acordo com os setores impactados pelo imposto do pecado de manter a atual carga tributária incidente sobre os produtos.

Como o I mposto eletivo tem noventena, ou seja, demora 90 dias para entrar em vigor depois de ser aprovado pelo Legislativo, o ministro informou que também combinou com os setores que, nesse meio tempo, provavelmente até fevereiro de 2027, o Imposto Sobre Produtos Industrializados (IPI) continuará sendo cobrado sobre esses produtos — como forma de evitar perda de arrecadação.

🔎 Criado pela reforma tributária sobre o consumo, o imposto do pecado começará a ser cobrado em 2027 e tem o objetivo de encarecer produtos ou atividades que causam danos à saúde ou ao meio ambiente.

A lista inclui bebidas alcoólicas, refrigerantes e cigarros. O novo imposto também incidirá sobre alguns veículos, conforme o nível de poluição, sobre a extração de bens minerais e sobre loterias, apostas e jogos de fantasy sports. ( leia mais abaixo ).

Com a cobrança do Imposto Seletivo e da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), outro tributo criado pela reforma e que começará a ser cobrado em 2027, o governo busca manter a arrecadação estável em relação ao Produto Interno Bruto (PIB).

Dario Durigan, ministro da Fazenda — Foto: Washington Costa/MF

Veja alguns dos principais produtos afetados

➡️ Um levantamento da Fiocruz, citado pelo Ministério da Saúde, aponta que o consumo de álcool gerou custos de R$ 18,8 bilhões em 2019. Desse total, R$ 1,1 bilhão correspondeu a gastos federais diretos com internações e atendimentos ambulatoriais no Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). Outros R$ 17,7 bilhões foram associados à perda de produtividade causada por mortes prematuras, afastamentos do trabalho, aposentadorias precoces e licenças médicas relacionadas a doenças provocadas pelo consumo de álcool.

➡️ No Brasil, segundo o Ministério da Saúde, as doenças relacionadas ao tabagismo geram custos indiretos de R$ 86,3 bilhões por ano. Considerando também os custos diretos, o impacto econômico anual chega a R$ 153,5 bilhões, o equivalente a 1,6% do PIB. "Em contrapartida, a arrecadação de tributos federais na venda de cigarros é de apenas R$ 8 bilhões por ano, o que evidencia desequilíbrio entre os gastos com a saúde e a arrecadação gerada pela comercialização do produto", diz.

➡️ Em um estudo para embasar a cobrança do Imposto Seletivo, o governo estimou que o tratamento de doenças associadas ao consumo de bebidas ultraprocessadas , como refrigerantes, isotônicos e refrescos, custa quase R$ 3 bilhões por ano ao Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

➡️ Produtores nacionais afirmam que as bebidas alcoólicas já são muito tributadas no Brasil, com impostos que representam de 40% a mais de 80% do preço dos produtos. Segundo o setor, um eventual aumento da tributação pode reduzir as margens de lucro, elevar os preços ao consumidor, provocar demissões e estimular o mercado ilegal.

articles.title: Dólar opera em alta e bate R$ 5,51, com eleições nos EUA e juros no radar; Ibovespa cai aos 165 mil pontos | G1
articles.standfirst: Na sexta-feira, a bolsa brasileira recuou 0,75%, aos 167.922 pontos, no 5º dia seguido de perdas. Já a moeda americana fechou em alta de 1,05%, a R$ 5,4442.
articles.summary: Na sexta-feira, a bolsa brasileira recuou 0,75%, aos 167.922 pontos, no 5º dia seguido de perdas. Já a moeda americana fechou em alta de 1,05%, a R$ 5,4442.
articles.body:
O dólar opera em alta nesta terça-feira (3), com um avanço de 0,84% perto das 11h, cotado a R$ 5,4899 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, continuava em trajetória de queda, com um recuo de 1,60% no mesmo horário, aos 165.238 pontos .

Na última sexta-feira (30), a moeda americana subiu a R$ 5,44 e acumulou alta de mais de 9% na semana. Já o Ibovespa caiu pelo quinto dia seguido e acumulou desvalorização de 18,12% no período, na quinta maior perda semanal desde o início do Plano Real, em julho de 1994. Saiba mais.

O principal destaque da sessão fica com as eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos , conhecidas como midterms. Novos dados do mercado de trabalho americano e a espera pela nova taxa de juros brasileira, que deve ser decidida amanhã também podem mexer com os negócios.

▶️ As midterms são o principal destaque da sessão. A votação vai renovar quase todo o Congresso americano e é crucial para o presidente Donald Trump , já que pode determinar o espaço que o governo terá para aprovar medidas sobre gastos públicos, impostos e regulação.

Essas decisões também influenciam as expectativas dos investidores e podem afetar os juros e o dólar no mercado internacional. (entenda mais abaixo)

▶️ Com as eleições americanas na mira, novos dados do mercado de trabalho dos EUA também ficam no radar. O indicador deve trazer sinais sobre a economia no país e dar pistas sobre os próximos passos do Federal Reserve ( Fed , o banco central americano) na definição das taxas de juros.

▶️ Por aqui, investidores aguardam a próxima reunião do Banco Central, marcada para amanhã. Em meio à pressão fiscal e eleitoral, a expectativa do mercado é que o Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) mantenha a Selic inalterada em 13,75% ao ano.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Milhares de eleitores irão às urnas nesta terça-feira (3) para as eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, conhecidas como midterms. A votação vai renovar quase todo o Congresso americano e é crucial para o presidente Donald Trump.

Diferentemente do Brasil, o Congresso dos Estados Unidos é renovado parcialmente a cada dois anos. Quando ocorrem na metade do mandato presidencial, essas eleições são chamadas de midterms, ou eleições de meio de mandato.

Os deputados norte-americanos têm mandatos de dois anos, enquanto os senadores, de seis.

Com isso, a cada dois anos, o país renova toda a Câmara dos Representantes e cerca de um terço do Senado.

Sendo assim, em novembro, estarão em disputa todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara e 35 das 100 do Senado.

Nas eleições de 2024, o Partido Republicano garantiu maioria nas duas Casas do Congresso, mas por uma margem pequena.

O resultado deu base para Trump avançar com a agenda no Congresso, já que também é do Partido Republicano. Por outro lado, a maioria apertada limitou essa força e expôs divisões dentro do próprio partido em temas mais sensíveis.

Diante desse cenário, Trump tem investido pesado e feito promessas para tentar manter o controle da Câmara e do Senado.

O Ibovespa acumulou desvalorização de 18,12% na semana encerrada em 30 de outubro de 2026, após o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais.

Segundo levantamento da Elos Ayta, com dados da B3 , foi a quinta maior queda semanal desde o início do Plano Real, em julho de 1994.

O recuo igualou, com duas casas decimais, a perda registrada na semana dos atentados de 11 de setembro de 2001, quando o índice também caiu 18,12%.

As maiores baixas do período ocorreram durante a crise financeira asiática, em 1997 (-22,17%); a crise financeira global, em 2008 (-20,01%); e o início da pandemia de Covid-19, em 2020 (-18,88%).

Diferentemente desses episódios, a queda de outubro de 2026 teve como principal catalisador um acontecimento político doméstico: a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Segundo a análise da Elos Ayta, o resultado contrariou as expectativas de parte dos investidores sobre uma possível mudança na condução da política econômica e provocou uma reavaliação dos preços dos ativos brasileiros.

Em Wall Street , os três principais índices acionários americanos operavam mistos nesta terça-feira, conforme investidores seguiam atentos às midterms.

Perto das 11h, o Dow Jones tinha alta de 0,41%, enquanto o S&P 500 caía 0,51% e o Nasdaq Composite perdia 1,07%.

Na Europa , a maioria dos índices operava em alta. O DAX , da Alemanha, subia 0,17% no mesmo horário, enquanto o CAC-40 , da França, avançava 0,68% e o FTSE 100 , do Reino Unido, tinha perdas de 0,36%.

Na Ásia , as bolsas fecharam em queda nesta terça-feira, conforme investidores avaliavam as medidas para incentivar a entrada de dinheiro no mercado como insuficientes.

O SSEC , Índice de Xangai, perdeu 0,82%, enquanto o CSI300 , que reúne grandes empresas chinesas, caiu 0,20%. Na Coreia do Sul, o Kospi desvalorizou 3,59% e o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, teve ganhos de 0,57%. No Japão, o Nikkei permaneceu fechado.

articles.title: Copper, Tin Fall With Base Metals on Renewed AI Stocks Selloff
articles.summary: Copper and tin fell with other industrial metals, as a renewed selloff in technology stocks in Asia weakened the demand outlook for materials used in data ce...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Copper and tin fell with other industrial metals, as a renewed selloff in technology stocks in Asia weakened the demand outlook for materials used in data centers and to solder circuit boards.

Both contracts dropped more than 1% on the London Metal Exchange as concerns persisted over spending and stretched valuations at artificial intelligence companies. Tin has plunged 10% this quarter, the worst performer among the LME's six major metals.

Copper had risen on Monday, helped in part by a pullback in oil prices that could mitigate inflation pressures. The US and Iran have signaled a willingness to pursue peace talks, easing anxiety over the war's impact on interest rates and global growth.

Still, macro conditions are putting a lot of pressure on metals, particularly given the possibility that the conflict could resume after the US midterm elections, said Xu Wanqiu, an analyst with Cofco Futures Co.

Copper fell 1.2% to $14,180 a ton as of 10:50 a.m. in Shanghai, while tin declined 2.2% to $48,550 a ton. Aluminum dropped 1.1% to $3,060.50 a ton.

articles.title: 20 features of India's indigenous bullet train revealed: 280 kmph test speed, 249 kmph operational speed, 557 passengers, 8 coaches, Wi-Fi infotainment for Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed corridor
articles.summary: India's first indigenously developed high-speed bullet train, B28, has cleared an important stage of its safety evaluation and is undergoing the vehicle
articles.body: India's first indigenously developed high-speed bullet train, B28, has cleared an important stage of its safety evaluation and is undergoing the vehicle body shell assessment, commonly called the "squeeze test".The assessment was carried out at BEML's manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. The central public sector undertaking (PSU) is building the country's first two indigenous bullet trains, with each train consisting of eight coaches.Indian Railways is working towards starting trial runs of the B28 train on the 100-km Surat-Vapi stretch of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed Rail corridor by May-June 2027. Commercial services on this section are expected to commence in August 2027.What will be special about India’s first bullet train? What are the features that passengers can look forward to? We take a look:India’s first bullet train: Top 20 features you must knowDesigned specifically with Indian operating conditions in mind, Indian Railways says that the train combines engineering capabilities with domestic manufacturing expertise, while placing emphasis on passenger safety and comfort.Designed for a maximum testing speed of 280 km/h and an operating speed of 249 km/h.Total train length of approximately 202 metres.Eight-car configuration comprising four motor cars and four trailer cars.Passenger capacity of around 557, including dedicated space for two divyangjan or persons with reduced mobility. Information signage includes Braille to assist visually impaired passengers.Seven standard-class coaches featuring 3×2 seating and one executive-class coach with a 2×2 seating arrangement.Driver's cabs at both ends, equipped with an intelligent on-board control system to facilitate quick decision-making and coordination with the operation control centre.Two eight-car trainsets can be coupled to operate as a 16-car train in the future.Ergonomically designed seats with sufficient legroom.LED lighting throughout the interiors.Overhead racks for carrying baggage.Additional luggage stands on the floor for larger bags and suitcases.Power outlets for charging mobile devices and operating laptops.Modern bio-digester toilets designed to minimise effluent.Large windows alongside every row of seats, allowing passengers to enjoy the view.The train will also feature sealed, single-piece gangways connecting its coaches, enabling passengers to move between cars comfortably.LCD screens inside the coaches display information in English, Hindi and regional languages.Public address and automatic announcement systems provide audio information to passengers.Emergency talk-back units installed in passenger cabins and vestibules allow travellers to contact the train crew during emergencies.A Wi-Fi-based passenger infotainment system gives travellers access to preloaded entertainment and other infotainment content.Retractable steps fitted into the doors help reduce the horizontal gap between the train and the platform.The heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) system is designed to regulate the temperature and humidity inside the train, helping maintain comfortable conditions for passengers. Each coach is fitted with two HVAC units.Sound insulation within the car body and floor structure. Special coatings designed to dampen noise. Skirts, bogie covers and fairings that form part of the train's noise-reduction measures.It is also equipped with regenerative braking technology, which recovers energy during braking and helps improve overall energy efficiency.What is a squeeze test?The test examines whether the train's outer structure can bear intense pressure and external forces without suffering excessive deformation or structural damage in the event of a collision or crash.Officials familiar with the development said the exercise assumes particular importance because of the high speeds at which these trains will run. Their body structures must be strong enough to withstand substantial external forces if they are involved in an accident or collision.“After the successful completion of this test, the prototype should ideally be ready in less than six months. Since the B28 (Bharat 28) train is not being built on Japanese Shinkansen technology, the development process should not take much time. The squeeze test establishes whether the body retains its shape under pressure and whether the passenger compartment maintains its structural integrity,” an official told TOI.Earlier, while approaching the Cabinet for approval of the increased cost of the country's first bullet train project, the railway ministry had indicated that two prototype trains would be ready for trial operations in the first quarter of 2027.The ministry had also outlined the broader construction timeline for the corridor. The entire Gujarat section is expected to be completed by December 2027, while the full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor has a completion target of December 2030.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex ends over 1,200 points up, Nifty50 crosses 23,800; top 5 reasons for rally
articles.summary: Stock market rally today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 continued their winning on Tuesday after the stock market hit a 7-week closing high in the previous
articles.body: Stock market rally today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 continued their winning on Tuesday after the stock market hit a 7-week closing high in the previous session. Softer oil prices, rising expectations of a possible review of the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax structure and other supportive factors lifted investor confidence, leading to both major indices rallying over 1%.BSE Sensex ended the day at 76,917.85, up 1,225 points or 1.62%. Nifty50 closed at 23,810.85, up 370 points or 1.58%. The rally added nearly Rs 4 lakh crore to the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE, taking the total to Rs 486 lakh crore.IndiGo and HDFC Bank led the Sensex gainers, with both stocks advancing around 3%. UltraTech Cement, Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv and Infosys also rose by approximately 2% each. Reliance Industries was among the notable laggards, declining a little over 1% after recording a historic 12% jump in the previous session.V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that circumstances are ideal for the continuation of the ongoing market rally.“Decline in Brent crude to $104, further weakening of the AI trade, continuing flow of good Q2 results and FIIs turning buyers have potential to accelerate the ongoing rally. The 11.6% surge in a mega cap stock in one day is very rare. But this happened in RIL yesterday. Huge delivery based buying of around Rs 6413 crores, supported by excellent Q2 results, triggered massive short covering in the stock. Massive value buying along with big short covering leads to such sharp surges in stocks, even in megacaps. The takeaway from this experience is that patient value buying will be rewarded. It is possible that there are short positions in many quality large-caps. These are short-positions created by bears on expectations of continued FII selling. The circumstances are changing,” he says.“While the AI trade has slightly weakened, it is important to understand that this is only a correction, not yet a crash. Results of many AI companies continue to be good. So watch out for the trends in this segment. Results of the US mid-term elections due tomorrow and its impact on geopolitical dynamics will be keenly watched by the market in the coming days,” he adds.Why did the stock market rise today? Top reasonsExpectations of an LTCG tax review gather momentumHopes of a possible change in the taxation of equity capital gains gained traction after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday that the government would "consider" foreign investors' request for a review of the tax structure."The circumstances have changed and, therefore, the voices of concern are louder,'' she said at a media event, referring to reports that her administration had received suggestions to reconsider the levies on long-term capital gains (LTCG) for overseas investors."I quite appreciate that. So, I'll consider all this... Our growth is very important; where people are putting their very best, we are able to see sustained 7(%)-plus growth.''In a recent report, Jefferies said a potential reduction in LTCG tax could encourage foreign investors to return to the Indian market, which they have been steadily moving away from.Oil pricesCrude oil prices edged up marginally on Tuesday morning but continued to trade significantly below the levels of around $110 per barrel recorded in recent weeks. Brent crude futures stayed below $105 per barrel, while WTI crude futures remained under $97 per barrel.AI-related trade loses momentumApple announced its July-September quarter results on Monday, reporting earnings that exceeded expectations. The iPhone maker recorded a "revenue record", supported by sales of iPhones and growth in services revenue. However, higher expenses associated with artificial intelligence have raised concerns about pressure on profit margins.Apple CFO Kevan Parekh cautioned that gross margins in the final part of the year would moderate slightly from the 47.9% reported for the September quarter."We expect gross margin to be between 45% and 46%. This includes primarily the impact of higher memory costs, as well as some costs related to the ramp of Siri AI," Parekh said.Indian equities, meanwhile, are increasingly being viewed as an ‘Anti-AI’ trade. Consequently, concerns that the AI-driven market frenzy could lose steam are often seen as a positive for Dalal Street.Foreign investor buying provides supportForeign institutional investors (FIIs) continued to purchase Indian equities on Monday, recording net buying of nearly Rs 3,115 crore, according to provisional NSE data. The buying follows a period of heavy selling that had unsettled the domestic market.FIIs were net sellers through September and the first half of October. The trend reversed in the latter half of October, with foreign investors returning to buying. Their purchases have continued into November, offering some relief to market bulls.Rupee strengthens against the dollarThe rupee opened 0.26% higher at 94.6550 against the US dollar on Tuesday, compared with its previous close of 94.90.Commenting on the currency's outlook, Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst of Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said, “With the US election date approaching, markets will closely monitor whether the administration maintains this diplomatic stance or geopolitical tensions resurface. Lower crude prices could provide near-term support to the domestic currency. The rupee is expected to trade in a range of 94.50–95.25."(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: 'Punching below its weight': Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam vows to turn around airline profitability
articles.summary: Air India plans to increase its wide-body aircraft order as it looks to strengthen its international operations and improve its financial performance, CEO
articles.body: Air India plans to increase its wide-body aircraft order as it looks to strengthen its international operations and improve its financial performance, CEO Tewolde Gebremariam said on Tuesday while acknowledging that the carrier was currently “punching below its weight” in the international marke. He also expressed confidence in a turnaround, saying the airline's return to profitability would happen “very soon”."Air India has been punching below its weight, that will change," said CEO Tewolde Gebremariam.“I am more impatient than shareholders to see Air India turn profitable,” Gebremariam added that the airline had made significant progress in areas such as fleet renewal. However, losses, airspace disruptions and rising costs remain key concerns. “Cost per available seat kilometre is a major concern for us,” he said. He also said Air India would look at rebalancing its hubs and network amid the challenges. On India's aviation potential, he said the country could become a global hub if it did “the right thing at the right time”.Meanwhile, last month, Gebremariam set up a “multidisciplinary, cross-functional cost savings team” on a full-time basis to identify ways to reduce expenditure across the airline. Air India reported a loss of around $2.3 billion in 2025-26, its biggest annual loss since the Tata Group acquired the airline in January 2022. Its cumulative losses since the takeover have reached about $5.7 billion.In an internal communication to employees, the CEO called for a mindset of “frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making”, saying expenditure would be systematically reviewed across functions. He said that while many external factors remained beyond the airline's control, employees could influence how costs were managed through everyday decisions.You use AI every day. articles.title: Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited celebrates diamond jubilee year
articles.summary: The Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO) begins its Diamond Jubilee Year for 2026–27 on 3 November 2026, marking 60 years of work in
articles.body: The Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO) begins its Diamond Jubilee Year for 2026–27 on 3 November 2026, marking 60 years of work in cooperative development, agricultural transformation, technological innovation and improving the prosperity of millions of farmers.Established on 3 November 1967 with 57 cooperative member societies, IFFCO has grown from an ambitious cooperative initiative into one of India's major cooperative organisations.As IFFCO enters its 60th year, the organisation will pay special homage to its founder and first Chairman, Maharajkumar Sahib Udaybhansinhji Natwarsinhji Jethwa, whose vision helped establish the cooperative.As a gesture of respect, gratitude and remembrance, his statues are being installed at all IFFCO manufacturing units and at the organisation's head office in New Delhi to mark the commencement of the Diamond Jubilee Year.Six decades of IFFCOIFFCO's industrial journey took a significant step forward in 1975, when it established its first fertiliser manufacturing facility at the IFFCO Kalol Unit near Ahmedabad in Gujarat. The Kandla Unit followed in 1976, strengthening the organisation's role in expanding India's domestic fertiliser production.The cooperative continued to broaden its manufacturing footprint with the establishment of the Phulpur Unit in 1981 and the Aonla Unit in 1988. These developments further expanded its production capabilities and geographical reach.Another major milestone came in 2005, when IFFCO became India's first cooperative organisation to acquire a private-sector enterprise.The IFFCO Kalol Unit has been instrumental in the cooperative's expansion. A major capacity expansion in 1998 raised the unit's production capability to approximately 1,100 metric tonnes of ammonia and 1,650 metric tonnes of urea per day.The unit continued to focus on conserving energy, improving operational efficiency and adopting sustainable industrial practices. During 2011–12, it implemented an Energy Saving Project that delivered substantial improvements in energy utilisation and plant performance.Continuing this journey of industrial progress, the IFFCO Kalol Unit marked 50 years since its establishment in 2025. The milestone commemorated five decades of service to farmers, industrial achievement and contribution to the country's fertiliser industry.IFFCO also ventured into nanotechnology, ushering in a new phase in the development of fertilisers worldwide.In 2019, the organisation developed nano fertilisers indigenously and began field trials under the guidance of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).The initiative progressed further in 2021, when IFFCO's Nano Urea was formally launched for distribution across the country, with dispatches beginning for farmers.Marking the beginning of IFFCO's Diamond Jubilee Year, Dileep Sanghani, Chairman, IFFCO, said, “The Diamond Jubilee Year marks a defining moment in IFFCO's extraordinary journey of service to farmers and the cooperative movement. Over the last six decades, Today, IFFCO is proudly spearheading a new era of cooperative development by strengthening grassroots institutions, empowering rural communities, and promoting sustainable agricultural growth."As IFFCO begins its Diamond Jubilee Year, the organisation is reaffirming its commitment to building on its six-decade legacy.As part of a special initiative during the Diamond Jubilee Year, IFFCO's Board of Directors and senior leadership will travel across the country to participate in farmer gatherings and meetings organised by cooperative institutions.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: State Bank of India (SBI) on Tuesday reported a 14 per cent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 23,038 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 20,160 crore in the corresponding period last year.The bank's total income rose to Rs 1,43,796 crore during the second quarter, from Rs 1,34,979 crore a year ago, according to a regulatory filing, cited by PTI. articles.title: Gold, silver lose shine ahead of Dhanteras: Buy now, wait or invest in something else?
articles.summary: Sone pe suhaga, chandi hi chandi — Indian shoppers might just be having it all this Dhanteras!
articles.body: Sone pe suhaga, chandi hi chandi — Indian shoppers might just be having it all this Dhanteras!With Diwali around the corner, gold and silver prices have brought an early surprise for consumers. After a dazzling rally that took both metals to record highs earlier this year, prices have cooled off, giving festive buyers a potential window to make their purchases.And the timing couldn't be better! For Indian households, Dhanteras shopping has never been just about chasing a good deal. Buying sona-chandi is a generations-old tradition, deeply rooted in the belief that precious metals bring prosperity, good fortune and a little extra sparkle to the year ahead.But before you rush to the jewellery store, there's a catch.The metals have been on a roller-coaster ride, and with prices fluctuating sharply, buyers are now faced with a dilemma:Should you buy now, or wait for another dip? Is gold the safer bet, or does silver offer better value?Gold and silver prices: How far have they fallen?After a spectacular rally that took both metals to record highs on January 29, 2026, gold and silver prices have come crashing down, with silver taking the bigger hit.Gold, which touched Rs 1,75,231 per 10 grams, has slipped almost to below Rs 1.5 lakh levels. Silver, which soared to Rs 3,84,632 per kg, has lost nearly half its value and is now hovering around Rs 2 lakh per kg.Internationally too, the yellow metal has faced pressure around $4,000 per ounce, while silver has witnessed sharp swings around $50 per ounce.But what's behind the sudden fall?For starters, investors began booking profits after the record-breaking rally, putting downward pressure on both metals. Adding to the pressure, the US-Iran war pushed crude oil above $120 per barrel, fuelling inflation fears and concerns that the US Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer. Higher rates make non-interest-paying assets like gold and silver less attractive than bonds.Together, profit booking, higher yields and a stronger dollar have weighed on precious metal prices despite ongoing geopolitical tensions.Gold and silver: What's next for the shiny duoGold and silver have lost some of their shine lately, but is the worst behind us, or is there more drama ahead?According to Vedika Narvekar, research analyst of commodities & currencies at Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers, both metals could face a few more bumps in the short term, but things may look brighter down the road.Gold: Short-term pressure, long-term promiseThe gold could remain under pressure over the next one to two months too. The Fed's hawkish stance, inflation around 3.7% and Brent crude above $110 per barrel have raised concerns over further monetary tightening. US treasury yields near 5% and the dollar index around 102 could add to the pressure.Narvekar expects gold to trade between $3,950 and $4,200 per ounce internationally, or Rs 1,40,600–Rs 1,48,500 on the MCX.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();"We see international gold trading in the $3,950–4,200/oz range (MCX Rs 1,40,600-Rs 1,48,500), with downside risk towards $3,800 (MCX Rs1,35,000) if oil prices remain elevated and rate expectations harden," she told TOI.However, ETF inflows of around $10 billion in September and continued central bank buying could cushion a deeper fall.In the long-term, Narvekar remains bullish, targeting $4,900 per ounce, or around Rs 1.75 lakh on the MCX, by the end of 2027. Central bank diversification, rising US debt, fiscal concerns and possible future interest-rate cuts could support prices."A sustained recovery will require softer bond yields and a weaker dollar; until then, expect volatility rather than a quick return to record highs," she added.Silver: A bumpier ride ahead?Silver could face an even tougher road. Unlike gold, it isn't just an investment; it's also widely used in industries such as solar energy and electronics. That makes prices more sensitive to industrial demand, particularly as solar-panel manufacturers look to reduce silver usage.Narvekar expects silver to test $48–50 per ounce internationally, or Rs 1.70–1.80 lakh per kg on the MCX, amid elevated oil prices, rising yields and the Fed's hawkish stance.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();A gradual recovery towards $70 per ounce is possible in 2027, supported by electrification, electronics, data-centre demand and limited mine-supply growth. However, a return to January's peak of around $122 per ounce, or Rs 4.2 lakh per kg, appears unlikely."However, weaker solar demand, substitution and the possibility of a smaller market deficit could limit gains," Narvekar said.For investors, she advised caution rather than chasing a quick rebound."Investors should therefore treat silver as a higher-risk, higher-volatility holding than gold and accumulate in stages rather than expect a rapid return to peak levels," she said.Should you buy now or wait for a bigger dip?With buying gold and silver being a Dhanteras tradition, the recent fall in prices may come as good news for shoppers, especially as precious metals have consistently delivered double-digit returns through bull and even bear markets.But is it better to buy now or wait a little longer?Experts explain how to time your purchase, what to keep in mind and how much of your money to put into precious metals.Trying to time the market can be tricky, but waiting for a bigger dip could also mean missing an opportunity.Ayush Verma, director of Annapurna Jewellers Pvt. Ltd, Varanasi, said, “While precious metal prices may witness further short-term fluctuations, predicting the exact market bottom is difficult.”Buyers should prioritise affordability, financial needs and investment horizons instead of waiting indefinitely.Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar, views the correction as a natural pause after a sharp rally rather than a sign of a bigger crash. With research reports pointing to higher prices over the coming year, waiting for a steep fall carries risks.“Buying in moderation, rather than trying to time the exact bottom, tends to serve festive buyers better over time,” he said.For those buying purely for investment, Hetal Vakil Valia, jewellery educator, designer and consultant, suggests a measured approach.“Consider investing around 40% to 50% of your planned budget during Dhanteras and keeping the rest liquid,” she said.This allows investors to spread purchases over the coming months and potentially benefit from further dips instead of committing their entire budget at one price.For many, Dhanteras purchases are driven by tradition and sentiment rather than investment returns.Valia believes that the correction offers a more comfortable entry point for festive buyers compared with earlier record highs.Verma also recommends that those buying jewellery or coins for the occasion focus on affordability and personal requirements rather than chasing the lowest price.In short, investors may prefer buying gradually, while festive shoppers can prioritise their needs and budget.Your 101 guide to shopping gold and silverWith precious metals getting cheaper, filling your Dhanteras shopping basket might seem tempting. But from choosing the right metal to deciding between jewellery, coins, bars and ETFs, there's more to consider than the price tag.1. Gold or silver: Play it safe or chase bigger gains?If protecting wealth is your priority, gold may be the better bet. It's generally considered relatively stable for long-term wealth preservation and diversification.Valia added, “If you are comfortable taking on more risk in pursuit of higher returns, silver is worth considering.”But then, why choose just one?“A balanced approach could involve gold as the core precious metal holding, complemented by a smaller silver allocation for diversification,” Verma told TOI.This could combine gold's relative stability with silver's growth potential while limiting exposure to the more volatile metal.2. Jewellery, coins or bars: What's the smarter investment?Buying precious metals doesn't necessarily mean buying jewellery. For those investing purely for returns, coins and bars may be more cost-effective.Shetty said, “Coins and bars work out cheaper than jewellery once making charges and resale cuts are counted in, making them the better route for pure investment.”Valia points out that making charges can range from 10% to 20%, affecting resale returns.Jewellery, however, offers value beyond its price tag, from craftsmanship and heritage to gifting and personal enjoyment.So, while jewellery may suit festive and personal purchases, coins and bars could make more sense for investment-led buyers.3. Digital Dhanteras portfolioDon't want the hassle of storing precious metals? ETFs let you invest in gold or silver without holding them physically, while electronic gold receipts give you ownership of gold stored in approved vaults.“Gold and silver ETFs skip storage and purity concerns altogether, and suit buyers who want exposure without holding the physical metal,” Shetty said.However, investors should compare brokerage, fund expenses, liquidity and market risks.And while ETFs and electronic gold receipts are regulated by SEBI, not every digital gold product has the same regulatory oversight.4. Buying it for the bling ? Keep these tips in mindIf jewellery is on your shopping list, look beyond the glitter!Verma advises checking design, purity, hallmarking and transparent making charges before purchasing.Remember, the quoted gold rate isn't necessarily the final bill. Making charges and other applicable costs can add to your expenses, while resale terms can affect how much you recover later.Those buying coins and bars should also compare purchase costs and resale options.5. No thumb rule!Afterall, not every Dhanteras purchase needs to be an investment! Jewellery may be bought for wearing, gifting or passing down through generations, while investment purchases focus on potential returns.As Shetty explained, “Which metal makes more sense usually depends on the buyer's purpose rather than one being clearly ahead.”Ultimately, the right choice depends on whether you're shopping for tradition, enjoyment or long-term returns.How much gold and silver should you buyGold and silver can add some shine to your investment portfolio, but going overboard may not be the smartest move. And when it comes to the ideal amount to invest, experts have different takes.Verma recommends keeping around 5–15% of an investment portfolio in precious metals, depending on financial goals, risk appetite and existing holdings.Shetty suggests a more conservative benchmark. “Many financial planners suggest keeping gold in the 5% to 10% range, as a broad rule of thumb that varies by household,” he said.Valia recommends allocating 10–25% of total household savings to precious metals, depending on individual circumstances, with gold forming the larger share.“I would generally favour a 70:30 or 80:20 split between gold and silver, keeping gold as the larger component because of its relatively stable role in wealth preservation,” Valia said.However, precious metals should complement, not replace, investments such as equities, bonds, fixed deposits and cash reserves.The bottom lineWhether you're buying for tradition or investment, don't let the festive glitter outshine financial sense.Rather than chasing the perfect price, experts suggest spreading your purchases over time. As Shetty puts it, “Buying a little at a time helps smooth out price swings instead of committing it all at once.”If you're bringing home physical gold or silver, look beyond the price tag. Check purity, hallmarking, making charges and buyback terms.Prefer ETFs? Keep an eye on fees, market risks and regulatory safeguards. Avoid borrowing to invest!After all, while precious metals may help protect your wealth, they don't earn interest or dividends. So, before splurging on that festive sparkle, make sure your emergency savings, insurance and essential financial goals are taken care of.A little sona-chandi can certainly add shine to your portfolio, just make sure it doesn't eat up all your savings!(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. Palantir's ( PLTR ) stock is being heavily defended post-earnings on Tuesday, as shares sell off 6% pre-market amid a broader meltdown in the AI trade.

The Alex Karp-led software play hit all the bullish notes in the third quarter, unlike hyperscalers such as Amazon ( AMZN ), which have sparked a fresh tech stock rout.

Revenue growth accelerated to 96% from 93% last quarter. US commercial segment sales exploded 148% year over year. US government sales accelerated to 96% from 90% previously.

Sales and earnings beat elevated analyst estimates.

There wasn't much more Palantir could do here to fight off the bear raid on tech stocks !

"Looking ahead, the shape of this quarter is what reinforces our view that 2027 is the inflection year for AI monetization, and Palantir remains our top pick in software," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

articles.title: The economy is 'less K-shaped than you think' — and that's bad news for the Fed
articles.summary: Wealth is up for every income group, but the top took most of the dollars, and inflation won't budge.
articles.body:
Americans at every income level are richer than they were before the pandemic.

That's good news for households and a headache for a Fed that has watched inflation, excluding food and energy, run above its target for more than five years.

Picture the letter K. In a K-shaped economy , the top arm shoots up while the bottom arm slides down.

Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk says the bottom arm is holding up better than most people think. "New data from the Fed shows that the US consumer is less K-shaped than commonly perceived," he wrote in an Oct. 31 note , pointing to spending growth of about 4% to 5% a year for every income group since 2024. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

The Fed's wealth data backs him up. Household net worth is up more than 70% for every income group since early 2019, by Yahoo Finance calculations, including about 73% for the lowest-earning fifth and 85% for the top 1%.

Of the nearly $84 trillion in new household wealth, the top 20% of earners collected about $63 trillion, or three-quarters. The bottom 20% got about $2 trillion.

Kyla Scanlon, author of "In This Economy?", explained on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang Monday why the economy can look strong even when most people don't feel it. Citing University of Michigan survey director Joanne Hsu, she said, "Spending is one dollar, one vote, whereas sentiment is one person, one vote."

The dollars keep voting at the cash register, and that's the Fed's problem.

A consumer this healthy keeps inflation sticky

"Core PCE inflation is supposed to be 2%," Sløk wrote in a Nov. 1 note . "Unfortunately, it has been 3% for three years, and it is now moving higher."

Core PCE , the Fed's favorite inflation gauge, rose 3.1% in September from a year earlier and hasn't dipped to 2% since early 2021. Sløk estimated last week that about half of that inflation now comes from strong demand, the part higher interest rates can actually help cool down.

So how much cooling would it take? A lot. His model says the Fed would need to lift its benchmark rate to roughly 6.75% by the end of 2027, he wrote in a Nov. 2 note . That's nearly 3 percentage points above today's 3.75%-4% range and would be the highest since January 1991.

The Fed "may be further from its inflation goal than the market currently expects," Sløk wrote.

The next clue arrives with Friday's October jobs report, which will show whether hiring is still strong enough to keep a December rate hike on the table. And since the top of the K owns the most stock, a lasting AI sell-off could cool the big spenders faster than any rate hike.

articles.title: Apple just made twice as much free cash as Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet and Amazon combined: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Apple just had the biggest cash year in its history, and it didn't need to build a fleet of AI data centers to get there.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ) just had the biggest cash year in its history, and it didn't need to build a fleet of AI data centers to get there.

The iPhone maker generated about $136 billion in free cash flow — the cash left over after running the business and paying for buildings and equipment — in its fiscal year ended in September, according to its results Monday . That's up about 38% from a year earlier and well above its previous record of about $111 billion in 2022.

It's also roughly twice what Microsoft ( MSFT ), Meta ( META ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) made combined over their latest four quarters, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

Those four companies spent more than $600 billion on capital expenditures over the past four quarters, much of it on AI chips and the data centers to house them. Apple spent about $9 billion in its fiscal year. That's down nearly 30% from a year earlier.

That bill is now showing up in their cash. Amazon has burned through about $42 billion over the past year, a record . Alphabet's free cash flow turned negative in the third quarter, and the stock just had its worst month ever . Meta's went negative for the first time since 2012.

Apple, meanwhile, brought in about $145 billion from its operations on record revenue of about $479 billion.

"We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders," CFO Kevan Parekh said in the release.

For the full year, Apple handed back about $102 billion through buybacks and dividends. Even that couldn't keep up, so the pile kept growing. Net cash — cash and investments minus debt — rose to about $57 billion from about $34 billion a year earlier.

The September quarter was the slow one. Operating cash flow came in slightly below a year ago.

Wall Street has noticed. Apple has become the market's hedge against the AI trade , and the stock was up about 25% this year through Nov. 2. Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet ranged from a loss of about 11% to a gain of about 6%.

Apple isn't sitting out AI. Parekh said on the call that Apple will "significantly increase our overall investments in AI," mostly through research and development. He also said the cloud costs of running its new Siri will show up in what it spends to deliver its services. Asked whether Apple's spending was cooling after a heavy year, Ternus didn't budge. "We feel confident that we're spending what we need to spend to achieve our roadmap," he said.

articles.title: Pfizer increases annual profit forecast amid solid demand for blood thinner drug
articles.summary: Investing.com - Pfizer has lifted its full-year profit forecast, thanks largely to strong demand for its blood thinner Eliquis.
articles.body:
Investing.com - Pfizer has lifted its full-year profit forecast, thanks largely to strong demand for its blood thinner Eliquis.

Adjusted earnings per share is now forecast to be between $2.95 to $3.05, compared to earlier projections of $2.80 to $3.00. Wall Street consensus expectations had seen the outlook at $2.96, according to data cited by Bloomberg News.

The drugmaker also guided for $62 billion to $64 billion in annual revenue, up from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion previously. Estimates had called for $62.26 billion.

"The company's guidance takes into consideration our strong year-to-date performance, continued confidence in our business and progress with ongoing cost improvement initiatives," Pfizer said. Previously, the firm outlined plans to slash an additional $2.5 billion in expenses.

Third-quarter per-share income stood at $0.87, above forecasts of $0.73. Revenue for the period inched down to $16.58 billion, exceeding estimates of $15.87 billion.

Global sales of Eliquis jumped by 25%, driven primarily by higher net pricing in the U.S. as well as increased demand around the world. Pfizer noted that this was partially offset by competition from new generic options and price erosion in some international markets.

Sales of Padcev, a targeted prescription medication used to treat advanced or metastatic bladder cancer, also climbed by 55%.

New York-based Pfizer has been banking on the success of newer medications to help decrease its reliance on older blockbuster drugs, particularly COVID-related treatments which sent revenues soaring during the pandemic. Excluding COVID-19 products like Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenues grew 7% operationally in the third quarter.

Shares of Pfizer oscillated around the flatline in premarket U.S. trading on Tuesday.

articles.title: Will removing LTCG tax be the silver bullet to get foreign investors back?
articles.summary: India’s long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax has now become a pressing pain for investors and the ongoing flight of foreign investors is being closely
articles.body: India’s long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax has now become a pressing pain for investors and the ongoing flight of foreign investors is being closely linked to the country’s somewhat unique regime of taxing stock market gains.India stands out internationally for its move to tax capital gains in the same country where the profits have been made. Reports suggest that globally most major stock markets do not have such a tax or the gains are taxed in an investor’s home country.Major stock markets around the world such as the US, Singapore, Hong Kong, Saudi Arabia, UK, UAE do not have any such tax, according to a Reuters report.India’s stock market has not hit a new closing high in over two years now. But India’s LTCG is not a new thing. It was introduced back in 2018, and has since then evolved. So why is the ongoing exodus of foreign investors since last year being linked to LTCG tax?(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();What is LTCG and how does it work?In India, both domestic and foreign investors face the same tax rates and structure.The taxes for equity market investments are divided on the basis of what the government defines as short-term and long-term periods of investment.For shares that you hold for a period of more than 12 months, a long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax rate of 12.5% is applicable. An annual exemption of Rs 1.25 lakh applies cumulatively across listed shares and equity mutual funds.For shares held for less than a year the applicable short-term capital gains (STCG) is 20%.Apart from this sometimes levies like health and education cess, can increase the effective rate to 15% and 24% respectively.Additionally, investors face a Securities Transaction Tax (Set) that is levied on the value of ⁠each trade. This varies for cash equities and equity derivatives.The case for removing LTCGIndian equity benchmarks, Nifty50 and BSE Sensex are in deep red this year, In fact, they are set for their worst annual stress in over a decade. However, in the last two years MSCI’s Emerging Markets Index has actually seen a jump of 40%.So clearly India is out of favour with foreign investors who are selling here and buying elsewhere. The rationale for growing demands of LTCG removal stem from a need to make India’s post-tax returns more lucrative to retain investors’ interest.The noise around removing LTCG, especially for foreign investors, is growing. Recently, SEBI urged the government to remove LTCG for foreign investors. SBI too in its report has said that while the RBI has been taking all possible steps to thwart a seemingly difficult global playbook, there is an urgent need also by the government to address some of the long pending structural issues regarding capital inflows.“The government must seriously look into anchoring hot money flows into the equity segment by extending the holding period to say 2-3 years and abolishing the long term capital gains tax for equity,” SBI said in a recent research report.Experts believe that removing the LTCG tax could send a strong signal that India wants to remain competitive for global capital. Also, with slower and fewer outflows of capital, and possibly greater inflows, the rupee will likely stabilise.The government too seems to be receptive to this growing clamour. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that voices are being heard. Her statements on the issue have led to the stock market rallying in anticipation of some announcement.On Monday, she said that the government would consider the request on structure of taxes on capital gains on equities.“The circumstances have changed and, therefore, the voices of concern are louder,’’ she said. “I quite appreciate that. So, I’ll consider all this... Our growth is very important, where people are putting their very best, we are able to see sustained 7(%)-plus growth,” she added.Will reducing or removing LTCG make Indian stock markets more attractive?Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) took out $19 billion in 2025 and about $30 billion is 2026 so far this year. A significant part of this money was used by FPIs to invest in the AI trade.Experts believe that removing LTCG would improve India's relative tax competitiveness, particularly for foreign portfolio investors, as India currently imposes capital gains tax on listed equity investments while several competing Asian markets offer more favourable treatment to foreign investors.“Removing LTCG would reduce the post-tax return disadvantage and make India more attractive to global fund managers comparing investment destinations,” says Thomas Stephen, Director & Head - Preferred, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers.However, experts believe that taxation is only one component of investment decisions.For example, China offers relatively attractive valuations and exposure to technology, while Taiwan and South Korea benefit from strong semiconductor and artificial intelligence-related investment opportunities.“India, meanwhile, continues to offer exposure to domestic consumption, financialization, infrastructure and long-term economic growth. Therefore, removing LTCG could narrow the tax disadvantage but would not automatically redirect foreign capital from these markets into India,” Thomas Stephen tells TOI.According to Riaz Thingna, Partner, Grant Thornton Bharat, removing LTCG can help in multiple ways:Abolition or rationalisation of LTCG could provide a meaningful sentiment boost by improving post-tax equity returns.For foreign investors, it could make it more attractive to allocate additional capital to India. For domestic investors, it could strengthen the attractiveness of long-term equity ownership. So, it’s clear that it would certainly improve India's relative tax competitiveness.But, as Riaz Thingna points out: Global investors compare markets on a much wider set of parameters.“Removing LTCG would eliminate one disadvantage in India's post-tax return proposition and bring India closer to markets where foreign portfolio capital can receive more favourable capital-gains treatment,” he tells TOI.Why removing LTCG will help, but not solve the problemThe government collected approximately Rs 1.29 lakh crore in equity LTCG tax in FY25, compared with Rs 72,249 crore in the previous assessment year. STT collections were estimated at approximately Rs 32,000 crore in FY24, with a substantial portion coming from derivatives rather than long-term equity investments.But, these collection figures should not be interpreted as capital inflows lost.“The actual impact is through lower post-tax returns, higher transaction costs and potentially lower investor participation,” Thomas Stephen says.Several factors have been contributing to the outflows - it’s actually what many would call a perfect storm.Valuations in the stock market were seen to be high, then the regime change and resulting tariff related uncertainty in the US added to woes, the rupee has been depreciating (a cycle aggravated by foreign investors outflows!), the US-Iran war has resulted in crude oil prices crossing $120 per barrel, India does not have an AI-led story to show while other EMs and major stock markets have offered attractive returns.So, LTCG adds to the woes, but by itself is not the single-largest factor driving the flight. In fact, despite the Budget changes in LTCG announced in 2024, stock markets continued to hit fresh highs.Hence, removing it would help improve competitiveness, but all other factors could still be in place. After all, India continues to be the fastest growing major economy in the world with a strong domestic story. But that has not been enough to make investors flock to its stock market in the last two years.Thomas Stephen of Anand Rathi explains: Removing LTCG tax could improve sentiment and encourage foreign investors to reconsider their India allocations, but it is unlikely to independently entirely reverse the FPI selling trend.“The recent outflows have been driven by a combination of relatively expensive valuations, concerns over corporate earnings growth, rupee depreciation, elevated crude oil prices and more attractive opportunities in competing markets. However, tax reform can act as a positive catalyst, but a sustained reversal in FPI flows would require more attractive valuations, improving earnings growth and greater currency stability,” he says.In fact, Riaz Thingna says that while removing LTCG could be a positive step, it would not be a silver bullet for FPI outflows.“The immediate impact could, therefore, be positive, but the durability and scale of incremental flows would ultimately depend on earnings, valuations and the broader macroeconomic environment. The government may need to weigh any revenue loss against the potential benefits of higher foreign investment,” Riaz Thingna tells TOI.VK Vijayakumar sums it up: Scrapping of LTCG tax alone will not make India attractive. Ultimately investment will be determined by earnings growth.“India will have to deliver on earnings growth. Fortunately, after tepid earnings during FY25 and FY26, earnings growth is improving this year. Nifty 50 earnings growth of 15% is achievable in FY27,” he tells TOI.Finally, valuations, corporate earnings, the rupee, and global interest rates are likely to remain more important in determining the direction and sustainability of FPI flows. Tax rationalisation could certainly improve India's relative attractiveness, but it may not substitute for earnings growth and attractive entry valuations.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Social Security November payments: When to expect your next check
articles.summary: The exact date you can expect to receive your Social Security payment for the month varies from recipient to recipient. Here's who is eligible to receive pay...
articles.body:
